title: Unclear whether setting defer attribute on script tags guarantees execution in document order
body:
I'm opening this issue as recommended by `mike5w3c` on the #mdn irc. The issue is that from the current spec we weren't able to deduce whether multiple scripts with a defer attribute can be guaranteed to execute in the order in which they appear in the document.

```html
  <!-- other content -->
  <script src="first.js" defer></script>
  <script src="second.js" defer></script>
  <!-- other content -->
```

So for the above example, it's unclear whether according to the spec `first.js` will always be executed before `second.js`. Can we get this clarified so that we can add this to the mdn docs?

Quoting the conversation from #mdn for clarity:

> Hey maybe this has been asked before, but the docs on the defer attribute of the script tag don't mention explicitly whether defer does or does not guarantee execution order. There is a lot of documentation online that states that defer guarantees execution order. But since it isn't confirmed or denied on MDN it's a bit uncertain whether that's true.
> 11:13 | zippity | Docs page is here https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/script
> 11:14 | zippity | Originated in this stack overflow question: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/47011676/will-setting-defer-on-my-polyfill-and-other-scripts-guarantee-that-theyre-loade/47012106?noredirect=1#comment80971490_47012106
> 12:23 | mike5w3c | zippity: The relevant normative requirement is in the HTML at https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html#list-of-scripts-that-will-execute-when-the-document-has-finished-parsing
> 12:24 | mike5w3c | where the requirement is to go through the script elements in document order and then “he script's type is "classic", and the element has a src attribute, and the element has a defer attribute ... Add the element to the end of the list of scripts that will execute when the document has finished parsing”
> 12:26 | mike5w3c | and then that’s referenced in places like https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#the-end:list-of-scripts-that-will-execute-when-the-document-has-finished-parsing-2
> 12:26 | mike5w3c | > Spin the event loop until the first script in the list of scripts that will execute when the document has finished parsing has its "ready to be parser-executed" flag set
> 12:26 | mike5w3c | so that doesn’t seem to guarantee execution order
> 12:27 | mike5w3c | because a script at the beginning of the list might not have its "ready to be parser-executed" flag set yet, but one in the list after it might
> 12:28 | mike5w3c | in which case they are going to execute out of document order
> 12:29 | mike5w3c | but if you want definitive clarification, the best was to get that is to open an issue at https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues to ask
> 12:41 | zippity | Ok, thanks for the answer.
> 12:42 | zippity | So but once we have clarification, do you think adding this to the docs would be a good idea?
> 12:42 | zippity | For me it seems like useful info, and I'd expect it to be under script > defer
> 12:48 | mike5w3c | zippity: yeah, ideally if you take time to file an issue, maybe it will result in a note getting added to the spec
> 12:48 | mike5w3c | in which case, the MDN docs could be updated to reference that note in the spec
